title: The d-th syzygy of a module of projective dimension at most d is projective
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module and $d\ge0$ an integer such that $M$ has a projective resolution of length $\le d$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Let $e\ge d-1$ and let $F_e\to F_{e-1}\to\dots\to F_0\to M\to0$ be an exact sequence [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] of $R$-modules with every $F_i$ projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. Then $\operatorname{Ker}(F_e\to F_{e-1})$ (for $e=0$: $\operatorname{Ker}(F_0\to M)$) is a projective $R$-module. In particular (taking $e=d-1$ when $d\ge1$): if $0\to K\to F_{d-1}\to\dots\to F_0\to M\to0$ is exact with all $F_i$ projective, then $K$ is projective; and if $d=0$, $M$ itself is projective.

proof.text: Extract the bounded projective resolution P from [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. For i >= e+2, the inequality d <= e+1 implies d < i, so P_i is zero. Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.extMk_surjective represents every Ext^i(M,Y) class by a morphism from P_i; this morphism is zero and ProjectiveResolution.extMk_zero makes the class zero. Thus M has categorical projective dimension < e+2. This is the explicit eight-line forward computation from the resolution, not an application of the resolution/Ext comparison theorem.

Prove the auxiliary claim by induction on e, with n arbitrary: if S has e+1 arrows, projective objects except its last object, an epimorphic last arrow, and pd(S.right) < n+e+2, then pd(ker(S.map 0 1)) < n+1. For e=0 use the kernel short exact sequence and Mathlib ShortComplex.ShortExact.hasProjectiveDimensionLT_X₁ with the projective middle object. For e+1, drop the first arrow. The induction hypothesis gives pd(ker(S.map 1 2)) < n+2. Exactness [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] makes f = kernel.lift (S.map 1 2) (S.map 0 1) an epimorphism, by exact_iff_epi_kernel_lift. Apply the same Mathlib dimension-shift theorem to 0 -> ker(f) -> S.left -> ker(S.map 1 2) -> 0. Its kernel is isomorphic to ker(S.map 0 1): compose kernelCompMono with kernelIsoOfEq using kernel.lift_ι. Transport the dimension bound along this isomorphism. The dimension-shift theorem is Mathlib’s direct realization of the contravariant Ext exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-ext-long-exact-first-variable]. Every induction step and kernel identification is proved in the private helper kernel_dimension.

Apply the auxiliary claim with n=0 and the bound from Step 1. Mathlib projective_iff_hasProjectiveDimensionLT_one, the projective Ext criterion [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ext-criterion], gives categorical projectivity of the original first kernel. ModuleCat.projective_of_module_projective turns this into Module.Projective; the universe max u v ensures the required Small instance for R.

For the stated exact partial resolution, write d=e+1, discarding d=0 by hd. The tail of S.precomp j is exact and Step 3 applies to S. Exactness of its first short complex and Mono j give fIsKernel; uniqueness of kernel limits gives K isomorphic to the first kernel of S. Transfer projectivity by Projective.of_iso, the invariance assertion [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand]. For the separate length-zero assertion, P_1 is zero, hence P.complex.d 1 0 is zero. Its augmentation is a cokernel of this arrow; CokernelCofork.IsColimit.isIso_π makes the augmentation an isomorphism. Transfer projectivity of P_0 to M and then to Module.Projective.
